meta.titre: Support and Movement in Animals: skeleton types, antagonistic muscles and the elbow
meta.sous_theme: Types of skeleton and the action of muscles

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A trader in a market in Douala lifts a bucket of tomatoes, a fish swims in a stream nearby and an earthworm crawls through wet soil after the rain. Each of them moves, but each has a different kind of skeleton and a different way of using its muscles. GCE questions ask you to compare skeletons, to name the structures that join muscles to bones and to explain how muscles in pairs bring about movement. This course starts from the simplest skeleton and ends with the arm.

items: A muscle can only pull when it contracts; it cannot push.
Bone is hard because it contains calcium salts, while cartilage is firm but flexible.
A joint is a place where two or more bones meet.
Muscles get the energy for contraction from respiration.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Why animals need support and movement

A skeleton supports the body, gives it shape, protects delicate organs and gives muscles something firm to pull against. Movement allows animals to find food, escape enemies and find mates.

### Three kinds of skeleton

| Type | Example | Structure | Advantage and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrostatic skeleton | Earthworm | Fluid in the body cavity, held under pressure by muscles | Flexible with no hard parts, but gives little protection |
| Exoskeleton | Grasshopper (insect) | Hard outer covering made of chitin | Protects and reduces water loss, but must be shed (moulting) for the animal to grow |
| Endoskeleton | Fish, goat, human | Internal bones and cartilage | Grows with the animal and supports large bodies; muscles are attached outside it |

### Muscles, tendons and ligaments

Muscles are joined to bones by **tendons**, which are strong and hardly stretch. Bones are joined to each other at joints by **ligaments**. Because a muscle can only pull, muscles work in **antagonistic pairs**: when one contracts the other relaxes, and the second muscle pulls the bone back.

### Movement at the elbow

The elbow is a hinge joint, which moves in one plane only. The upper arm bone (humerus) stays still and the forearm bones (radius and ulna) move.

- **Bending the arm:** the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes; the biceps tendon pulls on the radius and the forearm is raised.
- **Straightening the arm:** the triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes; the triceps tendon pulls on the ulna and the forearm is lowered.

Cartilage on the ends of the bones and synovial fluid reduce friction in the joint.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks how an animal with a hydrostatic skeleton moves.
variantes.contenu_markdown: The body wall has circular muscles around each segment and longitudinal muscles along the body. When the circular muscles in the front segments contract, those segments become long and thin and push forward while the bristles (chaetae) at the rear grip the soil. Then the front bristles grip, the longitudinal muscles contract, the rear segments are pulled forward and become short and fat. Waves of contraction repeat along the body.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks how a vertebrate moves in water.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Blocks of muscle on each side of the backbone contract alternately, bending the body from side to side. The body and tail push against the water and drive the fish forward. Fins help steering and balance. A streamlined body reduces resistance; many bony fish also have a swim bladder that helps them stay at one depth.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for the uses of the human skeleton.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Support of the body; protection (skull for the brain, rib cage for the heart and lungs, backbone for the spinal cord); movement, by providing levers and surfaces for muscles; production of blood cells in the bone marrow; and storage of calcium salts.

sections.enonce_markdown: An earthworm is placed on moist soil. Explain how its body moves forward. *(5 marks)*

etapes.justification: The question is about how muscles work against a skeleton, so the type of skeleton must be named first.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The earthworm has a **hydrostatic skeleton**: fluid under pressure and two sets of muscles.

etapes.justification: Forward movement starts at the front end while the rear is held still.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Circular muscles in the front segments contract, so those segments become **long and thin** and move forward; the rear bristles grip the soil.

etapes.justification: The rest of the body must now be pulled up.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The front bristles grip the soil, the longitudinal muscles contract, and the rear segments become **short and fat** and are pulled forward.

etapes.action: Say how the movement is repeated.
etapes.justification: Waves of contraction produce continuous movement.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The two stages alternate along the body, so the worm moves forward steadily.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** The earthworm has a hydrostatic skeleton of fluid under pressure, with circular and longitudinal muscles in each segment. The circular muscles in the front segments contract, making them long and thin so they move forward, while bristles at the rear grip the soil. The front bristles then grip and the longitudinal muscles contract, making the rear segments short and fat and pulling them forward. These waves repeat along the body and the worm moves forward.

items.erreur_markdown: "The triceps pushes the forearm down to straighten the arm."
items.pourquoi_faux: A muscle never pushes. It can only pull when it contracts.
items.correction_markdown: The triceps **contracts and pulls** the ulna while the biceps relaxes.

items.pourquoi_faux: Muscles are joined to bones by tendons. Ligaments hold bones together at a joint.
items.correction_markdown: Tendon: muscle to bone. Ligament: bone to bone.

items.erreur_markdown: "Insects have an endoskeleton made of bone."
items.pourquoi_faux: An insect has a hard outer covering of chitin, which is an exoskeleton.
items.correction_markdown: Insects: exoskeleton of chitin. Fish and humans: endoskeleton of bone and cartilage.

items.erreur_markdown: "When the biceps contracts, the triceps contracts too."
items.pourquoi_faux: The two muscles are antagonistic: when one contracts the other relaxes, otherwise the arm could not move.
items.correction_markdown: Bending: biceps contracts, triceps relaxes. Straightening: the opposite.

items.pourquoi_faux: An earthworm has no bones. Its fluid-filled body and muscles act as a hydrostatic skeleton.
items.correction_markdown: Earthworm: hydrostatic skeleton, circular and longitudinal muscles, bristles for grip.

items.enonce_markdown: Name: (a) the tissue that joins a muscle to a bone; (b) the tissue that joins one bone to another; (c) the muscle that contracts to straighten the arm; (d) the type of skeleton of a grasshopper; (e) the material that makes up this skeleton; (f) the type of skeleton of a fish.

A girl pushes open a heavy door by straightening her arm. (a) Name the muscle that contracts and the muscle that relaxes. (b) Name the bone that the contracting muscle pulls on. (c) Explain why two muscles are needed to move the forearm up and down. (d) Name the type of joint at the elbow.
items.solution_markdown: (a) The **triceps** contracts and the **biceps** relaxes. (b) The **ulna**. (c) A muscle can only pull. One muscle pulls the forearm up, and a second muscle must pull it back down, so the muscles work as an antagonistic pair. (d) A **hinge joint**.

items.enonce_markdown: In an investigation, an earthworm moved forward 1.5 cm in each cycle of movement, and each cycle took 6 s. (a) Calculate its average speed in cm per second. (b) How far does it move in 2 minutes? (c) How long does it take to cross a path 1.2 m long, in minutes? (d) The same worm is placed on a smooth glass plate and hardly moves forward. Explain why.
items.solution_markdown: (a) $\text{speed} = \frac{1.5\ \text{cm}}{6\ \text{s}} = 0.25\ \text{cm/s}$, so **0.25 cm/s**. (b) $2\ \text{min} = 120\ \text{s}$, giving $\frac{120}{6} = 20$ cycles, and $20 \times 1.5 = 30$, so **30 cm**. (c) $1.2\ \text{m} = 120\ \text{cm}$, and $\frac{120}{0.25} = 480\ \text{s}$, which is $\frac{480}{60} = 8$, so **8 minutes**. (d) The bristles (chaetae) cannot grip a smooth surface, so the worm cannot hold one end of its body still while the other end moves.

items_markdown: There are three kinds of skeleton: hydrostatic (earthworm), exoskeleton of chitin (insects) and endoskeleton of bone and cartilage (vertebrates).
Tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.
Muscles only pull, so they work in antagonistic pairs: one contracts while the other relaxes.
Elbow, a hinge joint: biceps contracts to bend the arm; triceps contracts to straighten it.
The earthworm moves by alternate contraction of circular and longitudinal muscles, with bristles gripping the soil.
